title: Alphonse Picou, Dave Dupas and High Society clarinet
summary: He recalls Picou, says Dave Dupas was the first he heard play the High Society clarinet part, and acknowledges Bocquet and Sid DeVean.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: No. No. No. No. No. No. No. He was waking up on St. Charles Street there. I forget what number of the place now. He was waking up there on St. Charles Street up there at that time. Oh, I know thousands of piano players, but I couldn't call all their names. Yeah. But then they had, like, a long time. Before I started playing, there was hundreds of piano players around there and hundreds of musicians. And, like that old man, Pico that died there. Yeah. Old Alphonse Pico there. I remember him playing. But I was small when I heard him playing, you know, like Tiger Reg and High Society and all that. And I heard him, a fella taking it and playing that when I was little. And I played it myself after.
Do you remember who was the first one you ever heard play High Society, that clarinet part? Was it Pico or somebody else?
I heard Dave Dupass play on the clarinet. I heard Pico play that after, yeah. But the first one I ever heard played was Dave Dupass.
Do you remember George Bocquet clarinet player?
Oh, yeah, I remember Bocquet, yeah. I remember him. Yeah, I remember George Good. I remember George Bocquet, yeah.

Well, I know him too. I know Sid DeVean. I know Johnny Babe. I know Johnny Babe who could play cornet. Sid DeVean could play clarinet and cornet. I know. That's what I tell you. It would be hard now for me to tell you.
